note.question: How does transparency determine whether a socially responsible firm can separate from a profit-maximizing greenwasher, and which visible CSR instruments are used in equilibrium?
note.overview: This is a two-firm signaling and price-competition game explicitly solved as a PBE and refined to an undefeated/lexicographically maximum sequential equilibrium.

sources.quote: When the transparency level is low (α < αc), a. if the market is less competitive (t > tc), the equi­ librium type is pooling (i.e., the profit-maximizing firm 2 greenwashes and mimics the socially responsible firm 1); and b. if the market is more competitive (t ≤tc), the equilibrium type is costly signaling (i.e., the socially responsible firm 1 overinvests in the observable CSR activities and CSR advertising to signal its intrinsic motivation and separates itself from the profit-maxi­ mizing firm 2).
